note: Hardware capability profiles keyed by canonical manufacturer (see MFR_ALIASES in scripts/build-cameras.mjs). 'profile' is shown on map popups when the model isn't tagged (almost always). Sources: FCC ID filings, ISED REL, teardowns, vendor datasheets — see data/research/. Seed data; expanded from certification-database research.

Flock Safety.radiosSummary: Cellular, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios onboard — active hotspot; sniff-capable hardware
Flock Safety.notes: No Canadian police contracts; Canadian pins are likely HOA/private or mistagged.

Genetec.radios: Varies: SharpV fixed is PoE (no radios identified); Cloudrunner is LTE + GPS only — no Wi-Fi, no Bluetooth
Genetec.radiosSummary: No Wi-Fi or Bluetooth radios identified — least sniff-capable of the major vendors
Genetec.confidence: Cloudrunner confirmed (carrier device listing); SharpV datasheet
Genetec.notes: Canada's most-deployed ALPR vendor (Montreal). Canadian cloud hosting; no vendor-run cross-agency search network.

Axon.confidence: vendor docs + app store pairing docs; FCC grantee X4G
Axon.notes: Toronto and York Region platform (Fusus). Customer-set retention, no vendor limit.

RTX Corporation.radios: Tolling gantry sensors (transponder readers + plate cameras)
RTX Corporation.radiosSummary: 407 toll system hardware — reads transponders and plates for billing
RTX Corporation.notes: These are the 407's toll cameras, operator-tagged as MTO. Not police surveillance.

Axis Communications.radios: None — PoE wired only (typical for Axis fixed cameras)
Axis Communications.formFactor: Fixed IP camera, ALPR via analytics software
Axis Communications.notes: General-purpose IP cameras running plate-reading analytics.

Neology.radios: neoForce: unconfirmed; legacy PIPS TS-500 offered optional Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and internal modem
Neology.radiosSummary: Radio loadout unconfirmed (legacy PIPS units offered optional Wi-Fi/BT/modem)
Neology.confidence: partial (legacy PIPS docs; neoForce datasheet not public)
Neology.notes: BC provincial program vendor; BC deletes non-hit reads at end of shift.

Motorola Solutions.radiosSummary: Cellular, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth radios onboard (L6Q)
Motorola Solutions.notes: Vigilant/DRN parent — the commercial-collection outlier in the US.

Dahua.radios: None — Ethernet RJ-45 only; PoE+/12VDC/24VAC power
Dahua.radiosSummary: No radios — wired PoE. But vendor datasheet claims recognition of driver and front-seat passenger features
Dahua.formFactor: Fixed bullet, vertical pole mount, built-in IR
Dahua.notes: PRC vendor; banned from US federal procurement (NDAA s.889), FCC equipment authorizations halted 2022; still sold in Canada. Datasheet: 'supports recognizing... features of driver and front-seat passenger.'

Verkada.radios: None on LPR-capable bullets (CB52-TE/CB62-TE etc.) — PoE wired; cloud-managed
Verkada.radiosSummary: No radios on LPR models — wired PoE, cloud-managed (footage leaves premises by design)
Verkada.confidence: vendor docs (Verkada LPR guide + power requirements)
Verkada.formFactor: Fixed bullet (telephoto/wide), LPR as cloud analytics
Verkada.notes: 2021 breach exposed ~150,000 customer camera feeds. Separate CR63-E 'remote' line has LTE.

Leonardo ELSAG.radios: Plate readers: wireless alarm broadcast (~0.5 mi); SignalTrace sensor adds Wi-Fi/BT/RF capture by design
Leonardo ELSAG.radiosSummary: Vendor of SignalTrace — device-signal capture as a product
Leonardo ELSAG.formFactor: In-car, fixed, covert pole/barrel, radar trailers
Leonardo ELSAG.notes: See the antenna problem — SignalTrace pairs device signals with plates.
